AH-0MUWZ5GST003NMFQ halves the enemy `bulletSpeed` of the eight shipped archetypes
across the runtime CSV, `DEFAULT_ENEMY_CONFIGS` and the per-entity constants.

## Problem

Several deterministic bot micro-simulations are knife-edge calibrations: a subtle, legitimate gameplay tweak (e.g. the 1-5% gentler thrust-press reduction in AH-0MUYRJQE50021T4A) flips their outcomes because scores are dominated by discrete hit/bullet collisions.

During AH-0MUYRJQE50021T4A two tests had to be recalibrated:
- src/ai/style/evaluation.test.ts - synthetic human seed moved 7 -> 14.
- src/ai/framework/competent/competentBot.integration.test.ts - RUN_SEED moved 0x0b07 -> 0x0b16.

On the base behaviour, src/ai/style/evaluation.test.ts already regressed on 13/24 seeds, and the competent-vs-legacy AC6 test only wins in base because the legacy bot chaotically collides with bullets; without bullets the legacy bot scored higher (22 vs 20) on base.

## Goal

Make these tests robust rather than seed-picked:
- Aggregate competence/style comparisons over a set of seeds (e.g. assert the styled/competent bot is not systematically worse), or
- Compare on scenarios whose score is not dominated by discrete collisions.

## Acceptance criteria

- AC1: The style-match AC4 demonstration no longer depends on a single lucky seed (e.g. asserts over multiple seeds).
- AC2: The competent-vs-legacy AC6 test asserts an objective-based advantage rather than relying on chaotic bullet collisions.
- AC3: Recalibrating either test is not required by an unrelated small bot-feel tweak.
- AC4: Full test suite, typecheck and build pass.

## Goal

Add a persisted `shareTelemetryDev` boolean field (default **on**) to `SettingsRecord`, and
surface it as a dev-only toggle in `SettingsScene`. The setting is inert (ignored) when not in
dev mode.

## User story

As a player/operator in dev mode, I want telemetry collection to be controllable via a game

# Dev collection-on-by-default in stock dev mode

Child of **Dev-mode telemetry upload to dev server with automatic evaluation** (AH-0MVBHRLY8004BGDN).

## Goal

A stock `npm run dev` (no special env vars) collects the run's telemetry to the local JSONL
sink whenever the share-telemetry setting is on, and collects nothing when the setting is off
or in a production build.

## User story

As a maintainer, I want any browser playing the dev-mode game to automatically collect its run
telemetry, so the run can be evaluated without a manual export step.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `resolveEffectiveTelemetryConfig()` (with the settings-driven flag wired in) returns
  `recording: true` with sink `jsonl` when `import.meta.env.DEV` is true and
  `shareTelemetryDev` is true, with **no** `VITE_TELEMETRY_*` env vars set.
- In dev with `shareTelemetryDev === false`, recording is disabled — the game neither collects
  nor uploads (parent AC2). **Plan-time decision:** the setting is the controlling gate for dev
  collection; the env-var escape hatch remains available for production (where it still requires
  consent), and this ordering is asserted by tests.
- In a production build (`PROD === true`) behaviour is unchanged: recording still requires
  `VITE_TELEMETRY_ENABLED` plus the consent flag; `shareTelemetryDev` is ignored.
- `PlayScene._initTelemetry()` loads the persisted setting and passes the dev-collection flag
  into config resolution, so a fresh dev session records from run start.
- Unit tests cover the (dev/prod) × (on/off) matrix plus production-consent-unchanged regression,
  and the JSONL sink writes under `ai_hell_telemetry_jsonl` in the happy-dom test env.

## Minimal implementation

- Extend `src/telemetry/config.ts` (and `consent.ts` resolution) with an optional
  `devCollectionEnabled` flag derived from the setting; default `false` so existing callers and
  production envs are unchanged.
- Change the effective recording gate to `DEV ? (setting || existing-resolved-recording) :
  existing-resolved-recording`, keeping the consent path intact — the exact boolean composition is
  pinned by the tests above.
- Update `PlayScene._initTelemetry()` (~line 3872) to `loadSettings()` and pass
  `settings.shareTelemetryDev`.
- Tests in `config.test.ts`, `consent.test.ts` and the PlayScene suite.

**Key Files:**

# Dev-only upload endpoint with validation and storage

Child of **Dev-mode telemetry upload to dev server with automatic evaluation** (AH-0MVBHRLY8004BGDN).

## Goal

A Vite dev-only middleware accepts the game's upload, validates the body against the existing
recording reader, stores it under `recordings/session-<timestamp>.jsonl`, and rejects malformed
bodies with a 4xx **without writing anything**.

## User story

As a maintainer, I want the dev server to reliably receive, validate and store uploads from any
browser hitting it, following the established `configCsvPlugin` pattern.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `vite/plugins/telemetryUploadPlugin.ts` registers `POST /api/telemetry/upload` only for
  `apply: 'serve'` (mirror `configCsvPlugin`); tests assert it is **not** registered for a
  build/production server and that `plugin.apply === 'serve'`.
- A valid body (≥1 schema-valid JSONL record via `parseRecording`/`parseTelemetryJsonl` from
  `scripts/recording.mjs`) ⇒ 2xx JSON confirmation carrying stored path, record count and run
  count.
- Invalid JSONL, zero valid records, or an unsupported schema version ⇒ 4xx **and no file
  written** (assert the recordings dir is untouched).
- The stored file follows the existing `recordings/session-<timestamp>.jsonl` naming
  (mirror `scripts/record-session.mjs`), is collision-safe/timestamped, and `recordings/`
  remains gitignored (no committed fixtures).

  with 4xx before parsing/writing.
- The plugin is registered in `vite.config.ts` next to `configCsvPlugin()`.

## Minimal implementation

- Reuse `scripts/recording.mjs` `parseRecording` / `parseTelemetryJsonl` semantics for validation
  (no new parser).
- Tests run the middleware behind a real ephemeral HTTP server against a temp dir, following
  `vite/plugins/configCsvPlugin.test.ts` (`startServer` harness with `serve`/`build` modes).

**Key Files:**

- `vite/plugins/telemetryUploadPlugin.ts`
- `vite/plugins/telemetryUploadPlugin.test.ts`

## Goal

After a valid recording is stored, the existing human evaluation pipeline runs automatically,
**asynchronously** (spawned child process — plan-time decision resolving the parent's OPEN
QUESTION), producing the human balance report and companions, with start/completion logged. The
existing `npm run record` and `npm run evaluate -- --human` flows continue to work unchanged.

## User story

As a maintainer, I want balance statistics computed automatically from every uploaded dev
recording without blocking the game or the dev server.

## Acceptance Criteria

- On successful storage, the plugin triggers `node scripts/evaluate.mjs --human <file>
  --out <timestamped output dir under eval-output/uploaded/>` as a **spawned child process**
  (decision: avoids Vite SSR contention with the running dev server).
- The upload HTTP response returns immediately — the evaluation runs in the background and never
  blocks the game or the response.
- Child-process failure (non-zero exit, spawn error) is caught and logged, never crashing the

## Minimal implementation

- Serialise evaluations (or cap concurrency) to avoid unbounded child processes — plan-time

- Log start, exit code and summary line on completion.

Child of **Dev-mode telemetry upload to dev server with automatic evaluation** (AH-0MVBHRLY8004BGDN).

## Goal

Verify all parent acceptance criteria on a real dev server run and a production build, and gate
the parent's completion on the evidence.

## User story

As a maintainer, I want proof that the whole flow works end-to-end in dev and is unreachable in
production before the parent feature is accepted.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **Dev happy path:** stock `npm run dev` (no special env vars), play a run to completion;
  confirm a `recordings/session-*.jsonl` file appears, the background evaluation runs and its
  `human-balance-report.json` (+ companions) appear under the eval output dir, and the dev-server
  console logs the evaluation summary.
- **Opt-out path:** with the setting off in dev, confirm **no** new recording file and **no**
  upload request (game neither collects nor uploads).
- **Production check:** `npm run build` passes (incl. `tsc --noEmit`, `vite build` and
  `check-bundle-hygiene`); `vite preview` serves no upload endpoint; the enforcement scan (F1)
  and full project test suite pass via the project test skill.
- Evidence (screenshots/URLs, file listings, log excerpts, test output) is recorded as a comment
  on the parent work item with the final commit hash.

## Minimal implementation

- Manual dev-run + setting-off run + production build verification steps above.
- Run the full suite via the test skill; triage any failures into critical test-failure items
  per the triage policy.
- Record evidence and a completion comment on AH-0MVBHRLY8004BGDN.

**Key Files:**

- Evidence/logs referencing `recordings/session-*.jsonl`, the eval output dir, `dist/` bundle and test output.

## Dependencies

- F1–F7 (verification is the final slice).

## Deliverables

Verified acceptance evidence; parent ready for `in_review` only after this passes.

# Mini-boss reward: upgrade-or-unlock + locked pool

Defeating a mini-boss grants exactly one choice — upgrade any 1 owned permanent weapon/power-up by one level, or unlock a new weapon type from a ~50%-locked pool — applied through the existing permanent-level machinery (epic AH-0MVCC8XSS007P01Z).

## Acceptance Criteria

1. On mini-boss defeat, exactly ONE choice is offered via the existing choice overlay (`MineralChoiceScene` + `powerups/choice`), launcher-agnostic.
2. Option A upgrades any 1 owned permanent weapon/power-up by one level via the permanent-level machinery (`powerUpLevels.ts`).
3. Option B unlocks one weapon type from a data-defined locked pool; ~50% of the weapon/power-up catalogue is locked at Level 1 (invariant test).
4. Only one choice is consumed per mini-boss; the choice is applied for the run; unlocking persists to the checkpoint state.
5. Tests cover both options, the ~50% invariant, and single-choice consumption.

## Minimal Implementation

- Add unlock-state helper + locked-pool data (bias toward new/late items).
- PlayScene defeat → launch `MineralChoiceScene` with the upgrade-or-unlock option set; apply via `applyMineralChoiceReward`-style path.
- Tests for pool composition + choice application.
- Deliverable: reward loop.

**Key Files:** `src/powerups/choice.ts`, `src/scenes/MineralChoiceScene.ts`, `src/powerups/powerUpLevels.ts`, `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts`
**Dependencies:** PlayScene mini-boss integration (AH-0MVCRBISU006NUN5), and the final power-up/weapon catalogues so the ~50% locked pool is defined over the complete 16/16 catalogue. **Deliverables:** mini-boss reward loop.

## Goal

Replace the arena's fixed two-to-N-wave hostile reservoir (skirmish model) with the **shared campaign sequencer**: the arena builds the shipped campaign via `buildSequencedLevels(rows, defaultCandidatePool, { seed })` (honouring `fixed`/`curve`/`dynamic` generation modes), drives the shared `WaveManager` state machine, spawns from `planSpawns(seededRng)`, gates wave/level completion through `onEnemyDestroyed`, and emits the canonical `wave_start`/`wave_cleared`/`level_cleared` telemetry events so `waveReached` and `levelReached` become meaningful, non-zero distributions in batch reports.

## User story

As a game designer, I want a bot batch to play the same campaign the game ships (all levels/waves via the shared sequencer), so per-wave difficulty targets can be tuned from evidence instead of intuition.

## Acceptance criteria

- **AC1:** One arena run plays the shared campaign (all levels and waves of the shipped definition, including `fixed`/`curve`/`dynamic` generation modes) and emits real `wave_start`/`wave_cleared`/`level_cleared` records with the canonical payloads from `runTelemetry.ts` (`level`, `waveNumber`, `waveCount`); a batch report shows non-zero `waveReached`/`levelReached`.
- **AC2:** Wave/level progression is driven exclusively by the shared `WaveManager` (`beginGame`, `planSpawns`, `onEnemyDestroyed`) and `buildSequencedLevels` — no divergent copy of campaign, wave, enemy or ship stats in src/ai/eval/ (asserted by the existing duplicate-body/parity guards).
- **AC3:** The `dynamic` wave mode derives from the run seed exactly as the game does (buildSequencedLevels `{ seed }`), so two runs with the same seed produce the same campaign for byte-identical telemetry.
- **AC4:** The Level-10 boss trigger is treated as the end of the run (no boss/mini-boss simulation this round — fidelity boundary, parent Q2=a); the boundary is documented in code.
- **AC5:** Determinism preserved: same seed + config + policy produces identical records on the campaign path; run never reads the wall clock.
- **AC6:** Unit tests cover progression, canonical event emission, seed-derived dynamic mode, and the no-divergent-copy guard; they pass under Node/vitest headless.

## Key Files

**Key Files:**
- `src/ai/eval/arena.ts` — drive buildSequencedLevels + WaveManager; emit wave/level events
- `src/ai/eval/arena.test.ts` — campaign progression, event payloads, dynamic-mode seed tests
- `src/waves/WaveManager.ts` — shared state machine consumed by the arena
- `src/waves/sequencedLevels.ts` — shared campaign builder (fixed/curve/dynamic)
- `src/waves/Formations.ts` — static LEVELS skeleton merged by the builder
- `src/scenes/core/runTelemetry.ts` — canonical wave_start/wave_cleared/level_cleared event names
- `src/ai/eval/types.ts` — telemetry/types consumed by metrics (verify/keep)
data.title: Arena plays the shipped campaign through the shared WaveManager

## Goal

Model the mineral hold and the hold-full upgrade-choice loop in the arena using the **shared choice system** (`chooseOptions`/`randomChoiceStrategy` from src/powerups/choice.ts with the run's seeded RNG), so the arena emits `hold_full` and canonical `choice_selected` events and report `upgradesSelected` becomes a meaningful per-choice-id distribution. The bot picks among the offered options using the same seeded stream (parent Q1=a). Choices permanently affect the run (ownership context carried into later choice offers) via the headless-safe adapter identified in the spike child.

## User story

As the automated-balancing maintainer, I want the arena to exercise the same upgrade-choice flow the game ships, so per-upgrade balance can be measured from bot runs.

## Acceptance criteria

- **AC1:** A run collects minerals into a shared-model hold (`MineralHold` semantics: capacity, growth multiplier, overflow); when the hold fills, the arena offers options via shared `chooseOptions(3, randomChoiceStrategy, seededRng, context)` and emits `hold_full` with the offered option ids.
- **AC2:** The bot selects one offered option via the run's seeded RNG stream; the arena emits `choice_selected` with the canonical `{ index, id }` payload; a batch report shows non-zero per-choice-id `upgradesSelected` distributions.
- **AC3:** The reward is applied through the shared reward path (or the named headless adapter from the spike) so later choice offers carry accurate owned-weapon/power-up context (weapon-level/power-up-level options) — no invented option model in src/ai/eval/.
- **AC4:** Deterministic per seed: the same seed yields the same choice offers and selections (byte-identical telemetry).
- **AC5:** Unit tests cover hold-full triggering, canonical event payloads, ownership-context carry-over, and seeded determinism; they pass headless under Node/vitest.

## Key Files

**Key Files:**
- `src/ai/eval/arena.ts` — mineral hold, choice offers, selection, choice_selected emission
- `src/ai/eval/arena.test.ts` — hold-full, event payloads, ownership context, determinism tests
- `src/powerups/choice.ts` — shared chooseOptions/randomChoiceStrategy/buildChoiceCandidates
- `src/core/GameState.ts` — MineralHold semantics (capacity, growth, overflow)

- **AC6 (parent-AC2 traceability):** The bot makes upgrade selections through the shared upgrade-choice flow and `choice_selected` events are emitted; a batch report shows non-zero per-choice-id `upgradesSelected` distributions.

Verify the campaign arena path's three hard guarantees with acceptance tests, so the balance loop (AH-0MV8Q5EYE001R715) can trust the richer reports: byte-identical replay, config sensitivity (a `difficulty-curves.csv` edit or upgrade-definition edit measurably shifts the corresponding distributions for the same seeds), and no wall-clock/IO in the pure eval core (parent AC4/AC5/AC7).

- **AC4:** A guard test asserts the pure eval core (arena/metrics/engine) never imports a wall-clock or I/O module on its campaign path; campaign progression, upgrade-choice emission, single-source-of-truth, config sensitivity and determinism are all covered by unit tests (parent AC7 umbrella).
- **AC5:** All new tests pass headless under Node/vitest and run in the full suite.

## Problem

`implement.py parent` decides whether a child worktree contains work via `_git_path_has_changes()` (`skill/implement/scripts/implement.py`), whose docstring says it returns True when the worktree HEAD *differs* from the parent branch. A child worktree that is merely **behind** `dev` (HEAD != `dev`, but zero commits ahead and no dirty files) is therefore classified as "has changes" and `phase_parent` immediately runs `finish` on it.

Observed 2026-10-19 during the AH-0MVF3BESP005ZDAV epic:

1. `implement.py drive` started child AH-0MVF6XLBQ002GYWQ and its session was killed at the 3600 s timeout with a clean worktree (no edits, no commits).
2. While the drive was running, three unrelated commits landed on `dev`, so the child worktree was 3 commits behind.
3. `implement.py parent` reported `Child AH-0MVF6XLBQ002GYWQ has changes — running finish subprocess...` and ran `finish` on empty work. `finish`'s changed-scope selection was unavailable and fell back to a full-suite run (~10 min under load), which failed and reported `Failed to finish child`.

## Expected behaviour

A worktree with no dirty files and **no commits ahead of** the parent branch must be treated as "no work" (return the child as `next_child` for implementation), regardless of how far behind it is. The worktree placement guard should likewise not be affected.

## Suggested fix

- In `_git_path_has_changes()`, replace the "HEAD differs from parent branch" test with an ahead-count test (`git rev-list --count <parent>..HEAD` > 0) so behind-only worktrees are clean.
- Add a regression test covering: clean worktree at the fork base, clean worktree behind `dev`, dirty worktree, worktree with one commit ahead.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1:** A child worktree with no uncommitted changes and no commits ahead of the parent branch is not treated as having changes by `phase_parent` (covered by a unit test).
- **AC2:** A child worktree that is behind `dev` but has no local commits does not trigger a `finish` subprocess.
- **AC3:** Worktrees with commits ahead, or with dirty files, are still detected as having changes (no regression).

## Problem

`node_modules/.vite` accumulates orphaned `deps_temp_<hash>` directories whenever a Vite dep optimisation is interrupted or collides — at intake there were 98 (141 MB), now **95 dirs / 158 MB total in `node_modules/.vite`**. They are pure cache debris: each is a partially written pre-bundle. The epic's AC3 timing work is unaffected functionally, but the debris wastes disk, slows directory scans, and is evidence that dep optimisation is re-running/colliding (which is one source of the transform/import variance measured in AH-0MVF6Y29M005TEOG).

## Why this was not fixed inline

`node_modules` is **shared by every worktree on this host via symlink**; deleting the cache while another agent's suite is mid-run can corrupt that run. The producer rule 'never destroy another agent's work' applies, so the cleanup needs a safe, quiescent mechanism rather than an opportunistic `rm -rf`.

## Expected change

A small, documented, safe cleanup path — e.g. `scripts/clean-vite-cache.mjs` that:
- refuses to run when any `vitest`/`vite` process is alive (or requires `--force`),
- removes only `deps_temp_*` (never the valid `deps/` bundle or `deps_ssr`),
- reports bytes reclaimed, and
- is documented in `docs/dev/test-suite-timing.md` (cache-hygiene section) and optionally wired into `scripts/hygiene_check.sh`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1:** A read-only `--dry-run` (default) reports the orphaned `deps_temp_*` count and bytes; `--apply` removes only those dirs and prints the reclaimed bytes.
- **AC2:** The script refuses to delete while a `vitest`/`vite` process is running unless `--force` is passed, and is covered by tests (dry-run classification, refusal path) that do not require a real cache.
- **AC3:** Documentation states why the cache is shared across worktrees and why the quiescence guard exists.
- **AC4:** After `--apply` on an idle host, `npx vitest run --project unit` still passes (cache regenerates cleanly).

## References

- AH-0MVF6Y29M005TEOG — measured the transform/import cost and rejected the optimizer/isolate/pool variants; notes the collision evidence.
- `scripts/hygiene_check.sh` — the existing periodic hygiene report this could extend.

## Request

'Consider deleting tests that build audio' — evaluate whether the audio build/guard test suites should be deleted rather than bounded, given they are subprocess-heavy (they shell out to the ToneForge/audio pipeline) and their subject may already be enforced elsewhere (CI build, `npm run build-audio:verify`, `npm run build`).

## Current facts (measured 2026-10-19, load ~28, 16 cpus)

- `scripts/build-audio.test.ts` — **39.3 s**, 42 tests, 20 real subprocess spawn sites.
- `scripts/audio-balance-guard.test.ts` — **1.2 s**, 31 tests, 7 spawn sites (cheap; deletion unlikely to be justified on time alone).
- By contrast `scripts/compile-promo.test.ts`'s real-ffmpeg smoke was the group's 140 s floor and is being moved to a gated `e2e` type (AH-0MVFSNO0G00035AP).
- `npm run build` already runs `build-audio.sh` and `npm run check-bundle`; `npm run build-audio:verify` runs `scripts/build-audio.sh --verify && node scripts/audio-balance-guard.mjs` — so **both** suites' subjects are reachable outside the test run.

## Decision to make

For each suite, one of:
1. **Delete** — its invariants are fully enforced by the build/verify scripts (then say which script, and confirm the script runs in CI/release).
2. **Move to the gated `e2e` type** (the mechanism built in AH-0MVFSNO0G00035AP) — keeps the coverage available on demand without costing the full suite.
3. **Keep in the full suite** — only if the tests assert something the build scripts do not (e.g. hermetic fixture behaviour, error paths, balance invariants not checked by `audio-balance-guard.mjs`).

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1:** Each suite's assertions are mapped to the production script/CI step that would catch the same regression, or the gap is identified (`build-audio.test.ts` 42 tests, `audio-balance-guard.test.ts` 31 tests enumerated).
- **AC2:** A per-suite decision (delete / move to `e2e` / keep) is recorded with evidence, plus the resulting change to `scripts/` wall clock (before/after measured, load recorded).

## Failure Signature

- Test name: src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts > PlayScene — playable run (AH-0MU7305Z2003NII3) > AH-0MUJM746P000QAEO AC2 — a live asteroid persists across a level transition
- Failing commit: (not available)
- CI job: (not available)

## Evidence

- Short stderr/stdout excerpt (first 1k characters):

```
Tests 1 failed | 6065 passed | 10 expected fail (6076) — full-suite run (test skill --scope full) failed in two consecutive runs; passes when the file runs alone and under artificial host CPU load.
```

- Actual assertion failure (cached full-suite run, `.worklog/cache/c85c9e0325b819469fa8bfe1e7cab170/stderr.txt`):

```
 FAIL  |integration| src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts > PlayScene — playable run (AH-0MU7305Z2003NII3) > AH-0MUJM746P000QAEO AC2 — a live asteroid persists across a level transition
AssertionError: expected false to be true // Object.is equality
 ❯ src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts:1629:28
    1627|     expect(wm.level).toBe(2);
    1628|     expect(wm.waveNumber).toBe(1);
    1629|     expect(asteroid.alive).toBe(true);
```

The test walks all ten waves of Level 1 (loop over `wm.waveCount`), then
asserts the carried-over asteroid is still alive on Level 2 — the rock was
dead by then, i.e. it was destroyed at some point during the walk.

## Steps To Reproduce

1. The triage template's `pytest -q -r a … -k '…'` command does **not** apply
   to this repo: the suite is Vitest/TypeScript (`|integration|
   src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts`), and agent-initiated test runs must go
   through the test skill (`/skill:test`), never ad-hoc `vitest` (AGENTS.md,
   test-execution policy).
2. Reproduce deterministically on pre-fix code: seed the scene RNG in the
   `bootPlayWithAsteroid()` fixture with `createSeededRng(20261020)` — the
   level-transition test then fails on every run at
   `expect(asteroid.alive).toBe(true)` (`PlayScene.test.ts:1629`). Without a
   seed the heading comes from unseeded `Math.random`, so reproduction is
   probabilistic (which is what the two consecutive full-suite failures were —
   two bad rolls, not a timing condition).
3. Re-run the affected scope after the fix: `/skill:test --type full`
   (audit-accepted full-suite evidence) or `/skill:test --scope changed` for a
   faster loop. Single-file runs are not a sanctioned reproduction channel for
   this load-independent flake.
4. Capture full logs and attach to the work item.

## Root Cause (identified)

- `Asteroid` derives its drift heading from the scene RNG when no exact
  velocity is supplied (`src/entities/Asteroid.ts` constructor:
  `angle = this._rng() * Math.PI * 2`).
- `PlayScene.rng` defaults to `Math.random` (`src/scenes/PlayScene.ts:601`),
  and the public spawn seam `spawnAsteroidAt` passes no `vx`/`vy`
  (`src/scenes/PlayScene.ts:3685–3692`), so every asteroid spawned by the
  persistence fixture `bootPlayWithAsteroid()` had a random heading.
- Whether that rock survived the ten-wave Level 1 walk therefore varied run to
  run: a heading through the player's position (player collision destroys the
  asteroid — the shared enemy-body collision model), through the auto-fire, or
  through a lingering test bullet (`killNonAsteroidEnemies` leaves
  zero-velocity bullets with a 0.75 s lifetime) destroyed it before the level
  transition. Solo runs and the full suite consume different `Math.random`
  streams, so the symptom was "flaky under full-suite parallel load" even
  though load is not the cause.
- Deterministic reproduction confirmed: `setRng(createSeededRng(20261020))`
  reproduces the failure on every run (implement-session comment, 2026-10-20).

Fix (already implemented, currently **uncommitted** in the parent worktree
`wl-AH-0MVF6VZG9000AN6E-per-describe-boot-reuse-in-heavy-suites`): the fixture
seeds the scene RNG with a fixed seed (`createSeededRng(1)` — heading keeps
the rock clear of the player while retaining both x and y motion so the
"carried-over asteroid continues moving" assertions still hold) and stops the
live rAF loop (`game.loop.stop()`) so an unpredictable real frame cannot
advance the tick-driven tests between `await` points. Verified: the asteroid
subset (61 tests) and the full `PlayScene.test.ts` (247 tests) pass twice
consecutively.

## Coordination

This item is a child of AH-0MVF6VZG9000AN6E (Per-describe boot reuse in heavy
suites); the fixture fix currently sits in that parent's implement worktree
together with the parent's in-flight per-describe changes. AC1 below is
verified once that commit reaches `dev`. If the parent's scope is later
adjusted so the fixture fix no longer ships with it, this item must own the
fix in its own implement worktree (same change, same tests).

## Impact

Failing test detected by agent during automated run. May block PR creation for the agent's current work item.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. The test `src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts > PlayScene — playable run (AH-0MU7305Z2003NII3) > AH-0MUJM746P000QAEO AC2 — a live asteroid persists across a level transition` passes when run against the latest `dev` (and keeps passing on repeat runs, not just once).
2. All related documentation is updated to reflect the change — at minimum the fixture contract comment in `src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts` (deterministic asteroid fixtures must be seeded / RNG-injected, never `Math.random`-backed). Product docs are unaffected (test-only change).
3. Full project test suite passes with the new changes (`/skill:test --type full`).
4. The remediation is deterministic — no `retry`, `skip`, `expected fail`, timeout inflation, or test deletion is used to mask the flake. The persistence fixtures seed the scene RNG and the tick-driven helpers remain the only way the scene advances between assertions.
5. A deterministic reproduction of the pre-fix failure is recorded (seeded-RNG recipe above) so the regression is reproducible and verifiable.

## Key Files

- `src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts` — `bootPlayWithAsteroid()` fixture (root cause + fix location) and the AC2 level-transition test (~line 1612).
- `src/entities/Asteroid.ts` — drift heading drawn from `scene.rng` when `vx`/`vy` are absent.
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` — `spawnAsteroidAt` (RNG pass-through) and the `rng = Math.random` default (line ~601).
- `src/test/gameHarness.ts` — `bootScene` / `advanceGame`; the live boot-loop behaviour the fix compensates for (`game.loop.stop()`).
- `src/test/powerUpTestFixtures.ts` — `createSeededRng` helper used by the fix.

## Suggested Triage Steps

1. Verify flakiness: rerun CI/test locally once.
2. If reproducible, assign to `Build` and route for triage.
3. If flaky, tag `flaky` and route to flaky-test queue.

## Suspected Owner

Build (confidence: 0.0, reason: no owner inference available — triage template default; the observed cause is a test-fixture RNG bug, owner: tests/build)

## Links

- Runbook: skill/triage/resources/runbook-test-failure.md
- CI artifacts: (not available)
- Cached failing run: `.worklog/cache/c85c9e0325b819469fa8bfe1e7cab170/` (stderr has the assertion, stdout the summary)

## Assumptions (recorded)

- **Fix lands via the parent item** (AH-0MVF6VZG9000AN6E): the fixture fix already exists uncommitted in the parent's worktree; AC1 is satisfied when that commit lands on `dev`. If it does not land with the parent, the implement phase for this item ports the same change into its own worktree.
- **Root cause is RNG, not load**: consistent with the evidence (fails twice consecutively in the full suite — two unlucky `Math.random` draws — passes alone / under artificial load by chance) and with the deterministic reproduction.
- **Gym parity unaffected**: test-harness/fixture change only; no gameplay code changes, so no gym scene diverges.

## Plan: changelog

- 2026-10-20 — plan session (herdr downtime dispatch): effort/risk computed
  (Extra Small / Low → autoplan skip path for this item); six automated review
  stages run against the existing content; description augmented with the
  confirmed assertion failure, repo-correct reproduction steps, root-cause
  analysis, key files, determinism ACs (4–5), and the parent-worktree
  coordination note; AC coverage review returned `proceed` (no children
  needed); stage advanced to `plan_complete`.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

No interactive producer was available (downtime dispatch), so no questions
were put to a human. Research entries recorded in the same auditable form:

- **Q: Why did the test fail in the full suite twice consecutively but pass alone and under artificial CPU load?** — Answer (research + implement-session evidence): the fixture spawned the asteroid from the unseeded scene RNG, so the drift heading was a `Math.random` draw per run; the full-suite runs drew headings that sent the rock into the player / auto-fire / lingering test bullets during the ten-wave walk (`asteroid.alive === false` at `PlayScene.test.ts:1629`). Solo and load runs drew survivable headings. Load is not the cause. Evidence: `src/entities/Asteroid.ts` constructor, `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts:601` (`rng = Math.random`), `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts:3685–3692`, deterministic reproduction with `createSeededRng(20261020)`, cached run `.worklog/cache/c85c9e0325b819469fa8bfe1e7cab170/stderr.txt`.
- **Q: Is there an existing open/duplicate work item for this test?** — Answer (research, `wl search`): no open item covers this test name; the two closest completed items (AH-0MUH1LEDQ0064J78 — obsolete asteroid-accounting AC6 flake from the pre-persistence rule; AH-0MUNVVWWC0015JTM — generic PlayScene/Gym flake under load) address different tests/mechanics. Not a duplicate.
- **Q: Is the fix already implemented anywhere?** — Answer (research, parent worktree `git status`/`git diff`): yes — uncommitted in the parent item AH-0MVF6VZG9000AN6E's worktree (`bootPlayWithAsteroid()` seeds the scene RNG and stops the live loop). Recorded as a coordination note above; AC1 verified once it lands on `dev`.
- **Q: Does the repo's test runner support single-file reproduction?** — Answer (research, `run_tests.py --help`): no file-scoped flag; `--scope full|changed` and `--type full|unit|smoke` only. Hence the derivation of step 2 (deterministic seeded reproduction) and the `/skill:test` commands in the reproduction section.
